The anti-LGBT municipal-resolution wave (80+ municipalities and four state/province-level declarations as of March 2020) concentrated in particular parts of the country, so the absence of local findings here indicates thinner documentation rather than established safety. The country's framework governs this division: no hate-crime protection on sexual-orientation or gender-identity grounds (a March 2025 amendment bill referred to the constitutional court, hearings held July and September 2025), court-based and medically gatekept legal gender recognition, and national sources documenting a trans foreign woman held in a male-only guarded detention centre and a regional human-rights court ruling that denying a prisoner hormone therapy violates private life.
blindSourceSummaries: A legal-aid organisation's report (13-28 March 2024): a regional court placed a trans woman from a foreign country, taking hormones since 2018, in a guarded detention centre for male foreigners; the border-guard agency refused to move her or to deliver her medication, interrupting her hormone therapy for three months; she was released after the NGO's application citing health grounds (under the statute governing foreign nationals, its health exception).

A trans-rights organisation's report (16 July 2024): on 11 July a regional human-rights court held that the country's prison authorities violated the right to private and family life by denying a trans woman access to hormone replacement therapy while imprisoned (she had been prescribed hormones for almost two years; the prison gave no reasonable grounds for refusal); 8,000 in damages ordered; the organisation had already intervened in 2021; part of a growing regional human-rights standard on trans prisoners' healthcare.
